data.text:
LEILA, CHEL URGE SUSTAINED ACTION, INDEPENDENT ANTI-CORRUPTION BODY AT RALLIES

House Deputy Minority Leader Leila de Lima and House Assistant Minority Leader Chel Diokno on Sunday addressed thousands at separate anti-corruption rallies — De Lima at Luneta and Diokno at the EDSA People Power Monument — urging sustained, peaceful public action and pushing for an independent commission to investigate alleged infrastructure corruption.

De Lima denounced what she called brazen theft tied to flood control projects and urged citizens to maintain pressure through legal action and civic mobilization.

"Magandang araw po sa lahat except sa mga corrupt at ganid o sugapa sa pera! Hindi sila welcome dito," she said, accusing alleged perpetrators of enjoying ill-gotten wealth while ordinary Filipinos suffer.

She called for the passage of the Independent Commission Against Infrastructure Corruption (House Bill No. 4453) and asked the President to certify the measure as urgent, telling protesters to channel their anger into lawful demands for justice.

"Pakiusap ko lang po: Pag-alabin natin ang ating galit hindi para humantong sa dahas o karahasan, kundi para sa pananaig ng hustisya at batas," De Lima said, adding that those responsible must be pursued and punished through the courts.

At EDSA, Diokno said the visible corruption uncovered so far is only a fraction of what he believes was taken, citing estimates that place flood control projects at ₱500 billion and saying the true amount could reach ₱1 trillion. He outlined Akbayan's four demands: open the bicameral committee (bicam) probe, make lawmakers' Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth public, pass House Bill 4453 to give teeth to the proposed independent commission, and prosecute and jail those found culpable.

"Higit sa lahat, ikulong na 'yang mga 'yan! Mabuhay ang sambayanang Pilipino!" Diokno declared.

Both lawmakers stressed peaceful protest, the rule of law, and continued civic vigilance as the nation presses for accountability amid the ongoing flood control investigations.

data.text:
🔥 Manila erupts: tens of thousands protest over stolen trillions

The Philippine capital saw its largest protest in years with the “Trillion Peso March.”

More than 80,000 people — mostly students and activists — accused authorities of stealing funds earmarked for flood relief. The money vanished, while disaster damage remains unaddressed.

Protesters burned tires, threw stones and bottles, and stormed government buildings. Around 40 police officers were injured, and 17 people were arrested.

According to The Guardian, as much as $17.6 billion may have been stolen. Viral footage shows the lavish homes of officials.

The finance minister previously admitted corruption “eats up” to 70% of infrastructure funds. Protesters demand asset disclosures from officials and warn of new rallies if the government stays silent.

data.text:
Sa ika-53 anibersaryo ng deklarasyon ng Batas Militar, kinalampag ng nagsanib-puwersang taumbayan ang iba-ibang dako ng Metro Manila bilang paniningil sa nagpapatuloy na katiwalian at karahasan mula pa noong diktadura ng ama ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

Dumaluyong mula UP Diliman ang mga miyembro ng komunidad patungong Luneta, kung saan naitala ang mahigit 80,000 kataong kumilos upang kondenahin ang talamak na pandarambong at pagkitil sa karapatan sa ilalim ng administrasyong Marcos-Duterte.

Giit ni Rep. Sarah Elago ng Gabriela Women’s Party, kailangang patuloy na magkaisa at kumilos ang mamamayan sa harap ng tumitinding krisis ng katiwalian. “Hindi lang tayo matututo mula sa kasaysayan kundi ang sambayanang Pilipino ay handa ring gumawa ng kasaysayan,” ani Elago. “Kasaysayan ng paglaban, kasaysayan ng pagkakaisa, kasaysayan na dapat nang baguhin ang bulok na sistema.”

Upang ipagpatuloy ang pagkilos pagkatapos ng Baha sa Luneta, nagtungo ang taumbayan sa Mendiola kung saan naghihintay ang barikada ng armadong kapulisan. Tahasang ginamit ng mga pulis ang kanilang puwersa upang marahas na i-disperse ang mga dumalo.

Pinuno naman ng nagkaisang grupo ng mamamayan, katuwang ang simbahan, ang kahabaan ng EDSA-Ortigas para sa Trillion Peso March. Bitbit ang panawagan kontra korapsiyon, sinasalamin ng martsa ng 100,000 mamamayan ang People Power Revolution na nagpatalsik sa diktadurang Marcos.

#BahaSaLuneta

#ML53
